Subject: Acme - Audit logging / SOC 2 follow-up (post-demo)

Hi Sanjay / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today - great conversation and very helpful context on Acme's compliance needs. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary from the demo / call:
- SOC 2: Redwood Inference is currently in progress on SOC 2 Type II; Type I completed and Type II expected Q3 2027. We can share the Type I report immediately and Type II once available.
- GDPR / HIPAA: Platform supports data residency controls and we offer BAA for HIPAA-covered workflows.
- Audit logging capabilities (what we covered):
  - Admin activity logs (user/admin actions in Console: role changes, policy edits, account provisioning).
  - API request logs (timestamped requests, method, endpoint, response status, latency, and metadata).
  - Exportability: logs can be exported to S3 (customer bucket), sent via secure syslog, or pulled via our secure API.
  - Immutability & retention: append-only storage with signed manifests and optional WORM-style retention; default retention 90 days, configurable to enterprise retention policies (e.g., 7+ years).
  - Redaction & PII: request/response bodies are not logged by default. We can enable full request bodies for audit-only exports under strict access controls and encryption, subject to customer agreement.

Actions / next steps:
1) I attached a short audit-logging overview PDF and a vendor security questionnaire (filled stub) - please review.
2) Michael (cc'd) will join a technical security call to answer SOC 2 and controls questions.
3) Dev (cc'd) will prepare a sample log schema and an export demo (S3 delivery + sample manifest).
4) Sanjay / Priya - can you confirm the retention window you need, whether you require request bodies in exported logs, and whether you want streaming to an on-prem SIEM or S3 export?

Scheduling: I can get Michael and Dev on a 30-45m follow-up next week - let me know a couple windows that work or grab time on my calendar: https://calendly.com/marissa-redwood/30min

Thanks,

Hi Marissa - thanks for the summary and the materials. A few clarifying questions from our security team: 

1) Retention: we need logs retained for at least 3 years by default and up to 7 years for certain regulated datasets. Can Redwood support per-tenant retention policies?
2) Immutability: can you describe the immutability guarantees - e.g., are manifests signed, can logs be deleted by admins, and do you support WORM?
3) Logged content: do API logs include request/response bodies or just headers/metadata by default? If bodies are optional, what is the opt-in process and how is access controlled/audited?
4) SIEM integration: we prefer streaming to our Splunk instance (on-prem) over S3 pulls - do you support secure syslog or a forwarder?

If you can send short answers to the above it will help us with procurement. Also happy to set a security-focused session with your security engineer.

Best,

Subject: Re: Acme - Audit logging / SOC 2 follow-up (post-demo)

Hi Sanjay - quick answers below and I'll have Michael and Dev add technical detail on the call: 

1) Retention: Yes - we support per-tenant retention policies. Default is 90 days for hosted customers; enterprise plans can configure retention up to 7+ years and we support export/archival workflows. We'll document the config and policy in the follow-up.

2) Immutability: We use append-only (write-once) storage for audit logs and maintain signed manifests per export. Admins cannot modify existing log entries; deletions are subject to retention policy and require a documented request for accounts with the proper approvals. We also support WORM-like retention windows for regulatory needs. Michael will provide specifics on manifests and tamper-evidence controls.

3) Logged content: By default our API logs capture request metadata (method, endpoint, headers, user id, timestamp), response status, and latency. Request/response bodies are not logged by default. Full-body logging/export is available as an opt-in enterprise feature with additional controls: encrypted-at-rest exports, role-based access to audit exports, and audit trails for who accessed the logs.

4) SIEM integration: We support secure syslog forwarding and direct S3 delivery to customer buckets. For Splunk on-prem we can do secure/syslog or push via a small forwarder. Dev will prepare a short demo on secure forwarding.

Next steps from our side:
- Dev: prepare sample log schema + S3 export demo (target: demo by EOD next week).
- Michael: share SOC 2 Type I report now and an expected Type II deliverable timeline (Michael - can you attach Type I by EoD?).
- Marissa: I'll send the completed vendor questionnaire and a calendar invite for a security deep-dive.

I attached an updated vendor_security_questionnaire_filled.xlsx with our high-level answers; we'll fill in more detail after the security call.

Thanks - talk soon.

Marissa
